sub_scenario.family: rapid live troubleshooting leadership versus careful asynchronous incident analysis
sub_scenario.one_line: wildlife disease surveillance officer: lead only with both source and location inputs

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the outbreak linkage chart and closing stale entries.
The sample registry review wrapped early today.
I gave a park officer the published result for one tagged bird.
Did that define an outbreak route?
No, it was a routine confirmed finding.
Someone new shadowed me in the field epidemiology unit this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the migration alerts into one message before lunch.
I did a standard pass over the sample registry records this morning.
I corrected a collection date in the sample registry last week.
I archived last cycle's notes on the sample registry and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
The interagency call begins at 05:30, and rangers depart at 06:10.
No, they are fixed on the collection order.
A vendor call about the outbreak linkage chart ran long but ended well.
I walked through the field epidemiology unit checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the migration alerts.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the sample registry records and fixed it at the source.
I closed a routine migration alerts cycle without surprises.
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the migration alerts before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the outbreak linkage chart updates.
The laboratory match report has a 05:00 delivery slot, and the field portal accepts an overnight sightings map until 05:15.
Yes, those delivery windows are confirmed.
I compared two options for the sample registry tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the field epidemiology unit handover notes.
Under what circumstance should I agree to lead the next dawn collection decision?

query: Under what circumstance should I agree to lead the next dawn collection decision?

ev_A.fact: During a February waterfowl mortality investigation, I combined banding histories, laboratory matches, and wetland visits, proposed a narrow sampling route, and the field team confirmed the source marsh on its first day.

ev_B.fact: On an April avian-alert call, I led route selection from two nearby sighting reports and sent crews toward one corridor; later samples showed separate introductions, so the crews searched the wrong wetlands.

E1.fact: The interagency call begins at 05:30, and rangers depart at 06:10.

E2.fact: The laboratory match report has a 05:00 delivery slot, and the field portal accepts an overnight sightings map until 05:15.
